title: Lightning Safety — NOAA JetStream
claims: Count the seconds between lightning flash and thunder; divide by five for miles, or by three for kilometres. A 15-second gap means the lightning is 3 miles (5 km) away.

If you hear thunder, lightning is near and there is NO SAFE PLACE OUTSIDE: immediately move to a substantial building with electricity or plumbing, or an enclosed metal-topped vehicle with windows up.
Stay in safe shelter at least 30 minutes after the last sound of thunder.

If outdoors, never lie flat on the ground, never shelter under an isolated tree, and never use a cliff or rocky overhang for shelter; get away from ponds, lakes and other bodies of water, and stay away from conductors such as barbed-wire fences, power lines and windmills.
Positive lightning bolts come from the upper parts of thunderstorms and can strike up to several miles away; it does not have to be raining overhead for a strike.
Rubber shoe soles and rubber tires are not insulators and offer zero lightning protection.
